# Base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and EFA support for AWS on ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set MPI compilers as default C and CXX compilers
ENV CC=mpicc
ENV CXX=mpicxx

# Install build dependencies, clone, build, and install Kripke
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git && \
    # Clone the Kripke repository from the main branch and its submodules
    # The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to fetch dependencies like BLT
    git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    # Create a build directory
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake
    # Enable MPI for multi-node execution and create a release build
    cmake -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Move the executable from the build directory to a system location on the PATH
    mv kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source code to reduce image size
    cd / && rm -rf /opt/kripke && \
    # Clean up apt cache
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default command to the Kripke help message
CMD ["kripke"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke benchmark on an AWS ARM-based Kubernetes cluster.
# It is configured to leverage AWS EFA for high-performance networking and is set to run across multiple nodes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-aws-arm-multinode
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 4 to run across up to 4 nodes.
  size: 4
  # The number of MPI tasks to launch. Set to 1 to satisfy "run on 1 node" which is interpreted as a single task.
  tasks: 1
  # The main container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The operator prepends "flux run -n <tasks>".
      command: kripke
      # Always pull the latest version of the container image.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # This container is not a launcher pod.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  # Keep pods running after the job completes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Logging mode that will fail if there are any errors.
  logging:
    strict: true
  flux:
    # Disable the flux-view sidecar; Flux will run directly in the application container's pod.
    container:
      disable: true
      # Specify the ARM-compatible flux-view image for AWS ARM instances.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
    # Specify the architecture for Flux, required for ARM-based nodes.
    arch: "arm"

  name: kripke-aws-arm-multinode
  namespace: default
